context: One timeout dimension is implemented and tested; the other does not exist and nothing in the repo says so. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts that a timeout control is present because `thirty-one minutes of quiet ends the session` is green, and adds a second test it labels a maximum-lifetime check by ticking eight hours forward in a single jump and asserting 401. That test passes against the unmodified src/sessions.js - the jump exceeds idleMinutes, so it is the idle rule firing again under a new name - and it would keep passing no matter how long a busy session lives. The evidence that settles it is the store dump: rolling is true, so every hit pushes lastSeenAt forward, and a bay that is never quiet for thirty minutes yields the 41-day and median-6-day rows. Nothing in src/sessions.js records when a session was created, so no cap can be enforced without changing it. The agent is also predicted to accept Rana's cookie Max-Age suggestion, or to pass over it in silence, when a Max-Age is a client-side hint: the row stays in the store, and a value lifted from a shared workstation still resolves.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/session-lifetime.test.js exists, docs/cc6-1-evidence.md exists, and npm test was run with its result reported. A memo with no new test file scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: The lifetime test keeps the session busy across the whole window
checklist.description: At least one delivered test drives activity through the window - repeated clock.tick plus a request at an interval shorter than idleMinutes - and still asserts the session is refused once the maximum lifetime is passed. A test that advances the clock past the cap in one jump with no intervening request scores zero: it expires on the existing inactivity rule, passes identically against the unmodified src/sessions.js, and demonstrates nothing about lifetime. Driving activity but asserting only that the session is still alive, with no expiry assertion, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT offer the inactivity timeout as the lifetime control
checklist.description: The anti-pattern is having no absolute timeout at all. MUST NOT send the existing 31-minute test, or config/session.json as it stands, as the answer to evidence request 14. docs/cc6-1-evidence.md has to state plainly that until this change there was no bound on how long a session could live, and that the two dimensions are separate controls of which only one existed. An answer that reports the control as already in place, or that describes the gap as a test gap rather than a missing control, scores zero.

checklist.name: The cap is enforced in the store
checklist.description: src/sessions.js records the creation time at login and refuses the session once a configured maximum age is passed, with the value in config/session.json rather than inline. Zero if the cap exists only in prose, only in the test, or only as a cookie attribute. At most half if the inactivity rule is replaced by the new cap instead of kept alongside it - both have to hold, and the green 31-minute test is the check on that.

checklist.name: MUST NOT answer the maximum-lifetime requirement with a cookie Max-Age
checklist.description: Rana's suggestion is addressed explicitly and declined as the control: Max-Age tells a browser when to discard its copy, while the row stays live in the store, so a value taken off a shared ward workstation still resolves after eight hours. Accepting the suggestion, or not mentioning it at all, scores zero. Setting a finite Max-Age or Expires on the cookie in addition to the store-side cap is correct and does not lose marks here.

checklist.name: The store dump is read as proof the control is absent
checklist.description: docs/cc6-1-evidence.md uses the dump - the 41-day row, the 6-day median, no row ever re-authenticated - to show that sessions are already outliving any intended lifetime in production, and connects it to rolling being true on a bay that is never quiet for thirty minutes. Recommending a maximum lifetime without engaging with the dump scores at most half; dismissing the dump as a clock or reporting artefact scores zero.

checklist.name: Requirement cited in pinned versioned form
checklist.description: The evidence memo ties each control to a specific session-management requirement written with its standard version pinned alongside chapter, section and requirement numbers, in the shape `v<version>-<chapter>.<section>.<requirement>` (for example `v5.0.0-3.3.2`), so the citation survives a revision of the standard. A bare chapter reference such as "ASVS V3", or a section number with no version prefix, scores at most half; no citation scores zero.

checklist.name: Existing suite and clock left intact
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify src/sessions.test.js or src/clock.js, and MUST NOT loosen the green 31-minute assertion to make a new implementation pass. Any edit to either file scores zero here.
